Subject: Re: Service credit claim from Acme - need calc and approval

Karthik / Monica —

I reviewed the contract (see clause 4.2 SLA credits). Short version: Acme is within the scope for a credit because the incident caused measurable customer-visible downtime. Two items to note:

1) Eligibility formula in 4.2.a uses "Aggregated Monthly Availability" and caps total credits at 25% of the monthly invoice for the affected service.
2) Clause 4.2.d allows us to prorate credits by affected resources (they were using a mixed hosted/dedicated setup); we should use the ratio of impacted routes to their total committed throughput for the period.

Recommend the following approach to avoid disputes: produce a clear calculation spreadsheet (Grace) with three lines: minutes_of_downtime, monthly_total_minutes (30-day month), and prorate factor for affected routes. Present both the raw math and a rounded credit in dollars. If anything contentious, propose to offer 50% of the calculated credit as a one-time gesture to expedite closure (we can reserve that option for leadership).

-Markus
VP, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Service credit claim from Acme - need calc and approval

Team —

I've attached a working spreadsheet (credit_calculation_ACME-5312.xlsx). High-level summary of the numbers and assumptions used: 

- SLA target: 99.9% monthly availability (allowed downtime per 30-day month = 43.2 minutes)
- Measured customer-visible downtime this incident = 107 minutes (Monica confirmed)
- Excess downtime = 107 - 43.2 = 63.8 minutes (minutes eligible for credit if full-service affected)
- Prorate factor (impacted routes / total committed routes for the month) = 0.75 (Acme reported 3 of 4 critical routes impacted)
- Billable minutes in month = 30 days * 24 * 60 = 43,200 minutes

Credit % = (excess_downtime / billable_minutes) = 63.8 / 43,200 = 0.001477 -> 0.1477% of monthly invoice

Acme's monthly committed invoice for the affected services = $240,000
Calculated credit = 0.001477 * $240,000 = $354.48 -> Rounded to $354.

However, contract cap is 25% of monthly invoice; not relevant here given the small credit. Attached sheet shows both the raw calculation and an alternate approach if we apply the 50% goodwill reduction Markus suggested. That would net $177.

Please confirm: (1) Legal ok with calculation methodology and (2) Leadership sign-off to issue $354 credit and a short apology note. If approved, I will create a credit memo and route to Billing to apply to next invoice.

Attachment: credit_calculation_ACME-5312.xlsx
